title: StutterClear: Alex has something to say
logline: Alex (fictional) built an app that teaches travellers to read Japanese train signs. He stutters; it is how he speaks. Tonight he records his demo-day pitch, and his real voice travels through StutterClear: a WavLM model on an NVIDIA GPU, CrisperWhisper's verbatim words, NVIDIA Nemotron's meaning guard; tomorrow, live on the call, a buffer half a second deep, NeMo captions, word rescue and Magpie. The judges hear what he meant, on his terms.

scenes.title: Tonight: the take

steps.line: He knows exactly what he wants to say. Listen.
Every word was there from the start. It just takes longer to reach the listener.

on_screen_text: Why are train signs hard to read?
scenes.visuals: The film draws the clip credit at top-left (x 56-820, y 48-175) while the real recording plays: keep that corner empty during the clip. Layout: a glass recording frame (~1240x620) at x 96-1336, y 210-830, and on the right (x ~1380-1824, y ~260-640) a slide card 'Why are train signs hard to read?' Frame header: a small Avatar (~72 px) whose rings follow envAt(d.clip.env_before, playhead), 'REC' with a pulsing dot, and a tabular timer counting real seconds from 00:00 to 00:19 at top-right of the frame. Row 1, label 'WHAT ALEX MEANS' (MONO caps): d.clip.clean in SERIF ~42 px at ~22% white, fully written from the start (it may wrap to two lines). Row 2: the BEFORE Wave (d.clip.env_before, sky, ~1160x110), playhead = elapsed / before_s, dimAfter. Row 3, label 'WHAT HE SAYS': a kinetic echo stack: each verbatim word of d.clip.words pops in at its real start time s (spring); a repeat lands on top of the previous copy, offset (+14, -10) px, and older copies drop to 45% opacity ('they' x3, 'writ-' x2 then 'writing', 'and' x3, 'in' x2, 'l-' x3 then 'letters'); every spoken word is the same white, fillers in italic 'um'; nothing is marked wrong. Each kept word of Row 1 (the words with removed=false, in order, matching clip.clean) brightens from 22% white to full sky over ~8 frames when its spoken word ENDS (its e time): the meaning fills in exactly as fast as the speech allows. Bottom-right of the frame: a headphones icon (the listener) whose ring fills clockwise in teal with the playhead. Line 0 plays before the clip over the empty frame. After the clip the timer freezes on 00:19, Row 1 is fully lit; on line 1 'Every word was there from the start' Row 1 glows once (soft sky bloom, scale 1.02); on 'the listener' the headphones ring pulses. scenes.title: Every 20 milliseconds, every word

steps.line: On a recording, a WavLM model trained on NVIDIA GPUs scores every twenty milliseconds of his voice.
steps.say: On a recording, a Wave L M model, trained on NVIDIA GPUs, scores every twenty milliseconds of his voice.

steps.line: CrisperWhisper writes down every word, stutters included, so cuts land only between words.
steps.say: Crisper Whisper writes down every word, stutters included, so cuts land only between words.

on_screen_text: sound repetition · word repetition · prolongation · block · filler
CrisperWhisper · every word with its timing
9 stutters cut · 9 long pauses shortened · 0 words clipped
scenes.visuals: The take laid out as a score across the width (time axis x ~330-1824 for d.clip.before_s seconds), a 'Thorough · recording' pill at top-left. Row A (top): the BEFORE Wave. Rows B-F: ProbLanes with the real d.clip.probs (5 lanes, labels from d.clip.classes, dashed 0.5 threshold), revealed left to right during line 0 so the probabilities 'light up' (a bloom where a lane passes the threshold), tag 'WavLM teacher · 5 classes every 20 ms' with an NvTag-styled 'trained on NVIDIA GPUs'. At the start of line 0, a magnifier circle on one stutter shows FrameCells (one cell per 20 ms, ~40 cells) with a '20 ms' label, then shrinks away. On 'so cuts land only between words': brackets drop for every entry of d.clip.cuts in time order (~4 frames apart): ROSE brackets for the 9 stutter cuts (kind word_rep, sound_rep, interjection) labelled in plain words ('repeated word', 'broken-off start', 'filler'), their edges snapping into the gaps between word chips; the chips inside get a rose strike-through; GREY brackets for the 9 'pause' cuts labelled 'long pause shortened'. Light snap sounds for the rose ones only. End on a counter chip: '9 stutters cut · 9 long pauses shortened · 0 words clipped' (compute the counts from the data).

scenes.title: Some repeats are meant

steps.line: Not every repeat is a stutter.
NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super, on Nebius, reads each cut in its sentence, as text only.
steps.say: NVIDIA Nemotron Three Super, on Nebius, reads each cut in its sentence, as text only.

steps.line: 'That that' is grammar. 'Very very' is emphasis. Both stay.

on_screen_text: on the laptop | Nebius Token Factory
On Alex's take: Nemotron checked 11 words marked for cutting · all real stutters

Required, bottom-left, from about line 2 on: a chip 'On Alex's take: Nemotron checked 11 words marked for cutting · all real stutters' (from d.clip.guard.checked and its empty kept list).

scenes.title: Demo day: half a second behind

steps.line: Demo day. On a live video call, Alex picks Gentle mode.
His voice waits in a buffer, half a second behind him, while WavLM-Large checks it on the laptop's NVIDIA GPU.
steps.say: His voice waits in a buffer, half a second behind him, while Wave L M Large checks it on the laptop's NVIDIA GPU.

on_screen_text: Removes clear repeats. About 0.5 s behind you.
4 s of past audio + 200 ms lookahead (Strong: 500 ms)
lookahead 200 · hop 160 · GPU + margin 100 · headroom 80 = 0.54 s

About 0.5 s behind you.', roughly x 330-1100, y 200-500): a cursor taps 'Gentle' on 'picks Gentle'. Line 1: the camera pushes into Alex's tile and it opens into the live pipeline (left to right, y ~330-760): 'Microphone · 16 kHz' emits his voice as 20 ms frame tiles (FlowPath kind frame) into a delay buffer drawn as a circle with frames orbiting it: a write head (sky dot) leads, a play head (teal dot) trails it by an arc labelled '≈0.5 s · Gentle' with a ghost dashed arc '≈0.85 s · Strong'. A bracket lifts a window off the stream: '4 s of past audio + 200 ms lookahead (Strong: 500 ms)'. Into the GPU Block (nv, accent C.nv, active while it works): title 'WavLM-Large · 316M parameters', model '25 layers mixed → BiGRU → 5 classes', where 'RTX 4050 laptop GPU · CUDA'. Under the Block: a timing ruler 0-160 ms with a filled 60 ms segment 'one window ≈ 60 ms' that re-fires every 160 ms ('re-run every 160 ms'), and a delay-budget bar to scale: 'lookahead 200 | hop 160 | GPU + margin 100 | headroom 80' = '≈0.54 s Gentle', with a thinner Strong row (500 | 160 | 100 | 80 = ≈0.84 s). scenes.title: Out to the call

steps.line: When a stutter's score crosses its threshold, a cut opens, and the stutter is skipped before anyone hears it.
A virtual mic carries his voice into the call, and NVIDIA NeMo captions what the listener hears.
steps.say: A virtual mic carries his voice into the call, and NVIDIA Nemo captions what the listener hears.

on_screen_text: NVIDIA NeMo streaming FastConformer · 480 ms chunks · int8 ONNX · CPU
Audio stays on this laptop. Nothing is recorded unless you switch saving on.
scenes.visuals: Continues the pipeline to the right (start as if the camera had panned from the previous scene). Line 0: one lane magnified (~900x180, a schematic curve) between a dashed 'open' line and a lower dashed 'close' line: when the curve crosses 'open', a rose bracket opens on the frame stream beneath; when it falls under 'close', it closes; two nearby brackets slide together ('close cuts merge'); an amber marker 'block: reported, never cut' on a separate stretch. On 'skipped before anyone hears it': the stream reaches the play head; the rose-bracketed frames lift out and fall away before it ('skipped before playback', a snap), the rest slide together through a short crossfade, and a fine teal-grey shimmer fills the join ('room tone, never silence'). Line 1: the cleaned voice (Ribbon) flows into a 'virtual microphone' node ('CABLE Input → CABLE Output') and fans out to three chips 'Zoom', 'Google Meet', 'Microsoft Teams'; the CallWindow slides back in on the right with a caption strip typing under Alex's tile in 480 ms bursts, tagged 'NVIDIA NeMo streaming FastConformer · 480 ms chunks · int8 ONNX · CPU' (NvTag). scenes.title: When a word won't come

steps.line: Then a word won't come.
Nemotron reads the caption and his context card, as text, and suggests the word he means.
He can say it himself, or tap it, and NVIDIA Magpie says it in a synthetic voice.

scenes.visuals: The call fills the frame: Alex's tile large on the left (~1000x560), three judge tiles stacked on the right. Under Alex's tile, the SHARED caption strip (NeMo) types d.rescue.said in 480 ms bursts and stops after 'Roman'. Line 0 'Then a word won't come': the stuck sound appears ONLY in Alex's private StutterClear panel (a small glass panel at the bottom-left labelled 'Only Alex sees this'): 'l–' with a blinking caret and the app's own amber status 'Pause kept. Take your time.'; the Avatar's rings tint amber (struggle) and slow. Line 1: two violet text packets leave the laptop side and cross a dashed 'text only · never audio' line to a Nemotron node at the right edge: one from the caption strip (the caption text), one from a 'Context card' chip showing d.rescue.context; the voice waveform stays on the laptop side. At the end of line 1, a 'Word rescue · Nemotron' card springs up in the private panel: the onset hint 'l…' and the three chips of d.rescue.suggestions, popping in one by one (pop). Line 2: on 'He can say it himself' the 'letters' chip glows; on 'or tap it' a cursor taps a 'Say it' button next to it (labelled with d.say.label); then the say audio plays (a violet waveform pulses on the button): the shared caption completes '...in Roman letters.' with 'letters' underlined in violet, the Avatar's rings return to sky, status 'Listening…'.

scenes.title: Measured on unseen speakers

steps.line: On seven speakers the models never trained on, live Gentle removes a third of stutters, and Strong two thirds.
Recordings remove ninety-one percent, and lose no words.

on_screen_text: Measured on 7 speakers no model trained on (UCLASS)
Teacher v2: macro F1 0.618 on SEP-28k-E
scenes.visuals: Header 'Measured on 7 speakers no model trained on (UCLASS)' (SANS 600 ~44 px) with 'stutters removed · words lost' under it. Three rows with equal visual weight: 'Live · Gentle', 'Live · Strong', 'Recordings · Thorough'; each has two bars on a shared 0-100% scale (~1100 px): 'stutters removed' (sky to teal gradient) and 'words lost' (rose), each ending in a Counter. Bars grow exactly when the narration names them: Gentle on 'Gentle' (33.1 / 3.1), Strong on 'Strong' (65.2 / 5.68), Recordings on 'Recordings' (90.9 / 0); on 'lose no words' the 0% gets a green ring pulse (chime). Footnotes (SANS 22 px, C.dim): 'Live delay ≈0.5 s (Gentle) · ≈0.85 s (Strong)', 'Recordings cut only between words', 'Teacher v2: macro F1 0.618 on SEP-28k-E'. Values from d.numbers.
